repo.description: Evidence-linked contest entry checks with NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory.

conflicts.explanation: R20 (S1) requires a video less than 3 minutes showing the project functioning on the target device. R78 (S2) requires a 3-minute or shorter public YouTube video showing how Nebius Token Factory and NVIDIA Nemotron were used. Both require a short demo video, but R78 specifies YouTube and explicit mention of Nebius/NVIDIA usage, while R20 is more general about device footage. The core requirement (short demo video) is aligned, but the platform and content specifics differ slightly.
conflicts.whatToDo: Upload a single public YouTube video ≤3 minutes that shows the project functioning on its target device AND explicitly demonstrates use of Nebius Token Factory and NVIDIA Nemotron/open models to satisfy both sources.

conflicts.explanation: R09 (S1) defines 'Runs on Nebius Token Factory or Nebius AI Cloud' as making a runtime call to Token Factory inference API or being deployed/run using Nebius AI Cloud compute. R80 (S2) states all submissions must run on either Nebius Token Factory or Nebius AI Cloud AND use at least one NVIDIA open source model. R80 adds a mandatory NVIDIA open source model requirement not explicitly stated in R09.
conflicts.whatToDo: Ensure the project demonstrably uses at least one NVIDIA open source model (e.g., Nemotron) in addition to running on Nebius Token Factory/AI Cloud, and highlight this in the video and description.

conflicts.explanation: R23 (S1) requires identifying which track you are submitting into (hard requirement). R79 (S2) says 'Pick the track that is the best fit for your project' (info). The project evidence shows track 'Best Apps and Agents' but S1's official rules may define specific track names (e.g., 'Coding and Agentic Engineering Track' per R51). There's a risk the track name used doesn't match S1's official track taxonomy.
conflicts.whatToDo: Verify the exact track names defined in S1 Official Rules and select/submit under the correct official track name; ensure the project fits that track's stated goal per R35.

topFixes: Upload a public YouTube video ≤3 minutes showing the project functioning on its target device with clear demonstration of Nebius Token Factory and NVIDIA Nemotron usage (fixes R20 fail, R21/R22/R31 actions, R78 hard requirement).

Confirm entrant is not a resident of prohibited jurisdictions (Brazil, Quebec, Russia, Crimea, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, or comprehensively sanctioned countries) and is at least the age of majority in their jurisdiction (fixes R02/R05 actions - disqualification risks).

Confirm the project is original work solely owned by the entrant/team with no third-party IP rights violations, and not derived from Sponsor/Admin-funded work (fixes R26/R34/R36 actions - IP/eligibility disqualification risks).
Ensure project is available free of charge without restriction for testing/judging until judging period ends (fixes R29 action - hard requirement).
If entering as a team or organization, appoint and authorize an eligible Representative; confirm all members are eligible individuals (fixes R03/R04/R27 actions - eligibility structure).
verdict: Submission passes core technical requirements (repo, demo, description, track, feedback, Nebius/NVIDIA usage) but fails critically on missing demo video and has multiple unverified eligibility/IP/legal obligations that risk disqualification if selected as winner.
